sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong commercial maritime and financial-law overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) with Investment Chapter, in force 2012

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework) as amended; Ley No. 70 de 30 de agosto de 2019 (Beneficial Ownership Transparency Registry and UBO filing obligations); Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations regime); Executive Decree No. 132 de 2017 (AML implementation regulation); regulatory instructions of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Private Interest Foundation Charter (Acta de Constitución and Estatutos)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the Republic of Panama / Registry of Private Interest Foundations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille at Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama or Panamanian Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate founder or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry / relevant foreign corporate registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authenticated passport copies for settlor, foundation council members, UBOs, and authorized representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly commissioned notary in the country of origin or Panamanian consular officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Wealth / Source of Funds declaration supporting the maritime bunkering capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Independent certified public accountant or external counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized declaration, apostille not mandatory in standard cases

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all direct and indirect beneficial owners, settlors, protected persons, foundation council members, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's national PEP database maintained by the UAF. The registered agent must assign an independent AML risk score using an internationally recognized screening engine (World-Check/Dow Jones). Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any individual connected to high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, arms, fuel, or maritime logistics sectors, and for any proposed bunkering counterparty lacking a valid Port Captaincy or Panama Maritime Authority operational license.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Módulo de Asignación y Reserva de Nombre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be written in the Spanish alphabet. Non-Latin script names must be rendered in phonetic Spanish transliteration. The registered name must include the suffix 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' and must be distinctive from all existing companies, foundations, trademarks, natural persons, and government entities in the Republic of Panama. Confusingly similar or misleading maritime names are not admitted unless ministerial or Maritime Authority authorization is produced.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested name is rejected, counsel must within 5 working days file an administrative reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) through the same public registry portal, attaching prior-use evidence or a notarized consent from the competing name-holder. If the reconsideration is denied, a further appeal (recurso de apelación) may be lodged within 10 working days before the Dirección General of the Registro Público de Panamá. A final administrative lawsuit (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the Tercera Sala de la Corte Suprema de Justicia must be filed within 30 days from notification of the second-level denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A private interest foundation may maintain a virtual or administrative office through a licensed Panama resident agent for passive asset-holding and procurement purposes. However, because the target scope is ship bunkering and fuel replenishment under ISIC 5222, any physical operational supply activity in Panamanian territorial waters will require a separate Maritime Authority bunkering license, a fixed operational address in Panama, and local staffing for compliance and spill-response obligations. A virtual office alone will not satisfy the shipping-license gateway.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% for Panama-domiciled bunkering and refueling operations; 20% for a purely foreign-flag bunkering procurement vehicle acting as a foundation without onshore maritime facilities; inspection probability rises to 85% following any AML compliance filing gap or sanctions hit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Private Interest Foundations are governed by Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Régimen de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Law No. 13 of 2017, and complemented by Law No. 23 of 2015 on anti-money-laundering due diligence. Relevant provisions: Articles 1-6 on creation, endowment, and purpose; Articles 7-12 on registered agent, name, and duration; Articles 13-18 on the Foundation Council and administration; Articles 19-25 on beneficiaries and the protector; Articles 26-33 on Public Registry filing, amendment, and merger provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Mercantile Section (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundational Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter), together with the Reglamento (Regulations), executed before a Panamanian notary and inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Article 6 of Law 25 of 1995 requires a minimum initial endowment of US$10,000, or its equivalent in Panamanian Balboas, declared by the founder in the Foundation Charter. The endowment must be subscribed and available at formation; the State does not require deposit into a government escrow account, but the registered agent must verify funding evidence. For active ship-bunkering operations, chartered banks will additionally require working capital or standby credit facilities above US$250,000 before opening transaction accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF THE PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION [FOUNDATION NAME], REPUBLIC OF PANAMA. We, the undersigned Foundation Councillors, convened under Law 25 of 1995, as amended, hereby resolve: One: to accept the Founder's subscription of the initial endowment of US$10,000 and issue the corresponding participation certificates. Two: to adopt the registered office at the offices of the registered agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama, with full authority to receive legal notices. Three: to appoint the Protector (Encomendado) and the following officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, with joint authority to execute bunkering agreements and open bank accounts. Four: to authorize the President to complete all Public Registry filings and to apply for the maritime bunkering license with the Panama Maritime Authority. Five: to adopt these minutes as the Foundation's constitutive governance act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Panamanian Registered Agent and Clear Client Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama-licensed law firm acting as Registered Agent (Agente Residente) under Article 7 of Law 25 of 1995
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a professional services agreement with a Panama-licensed attorney who will serve as the Registered Agent. Submit the foundation formation questionnaire, founder identification, and source-of-funds documentation for mandatory AML/KYC screening under Law 23 of 2015. The agent verifies the founder and beneficial owners, issues a written no-objection letter, and confirms the standard draft charter and governance package.
required_dossiers: Signed client engagement letter with registered agent
Private Interest Foundation formation questionnaire
Certified copy of founder's passport or national ID
Bank reference letter or source-of-funds statement
Certificate of good standing of corporate founder, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent requests further beneficial-ownership details, file a sworn declaration of the founder with supporting bank statements within 3 business days. If the agent declines the engagement, select an alternate registered agent with substitution of the engagement letter; no additional government fee is incurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Drafting of Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Certificate Section; drafting undertaken by the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a corporate-name search application through the Public Registry's Certificate Section or the registered agent's electronic portal. Upon issuance of the name availability certificate, counsel drafts the Acta Constitutiva in Spanish, incorporating the endowment clause, Foundation Council composition, object clause for ISIC 5222 marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment, and the confidential Reglamento with governance, beneficiary, and protector provisions.
required_dossiers: Name-search application form
Three proposed foundation names in order of preference
Foundation purpose and object statement for ship bunkering and lubricant supply
Declaration of initial endowment availability and funding source
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is already registered or conflicting, promptly file an amended application using the stated alternative names. The Public Registry normally waives any penalty if the corrected name search is submitted within 3 business days of the query notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (licensed Panamanian notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder or authorized attorney-in-fact appears before the notary, confirms the endowment declaration, and executes the Foundation Charter and Regulations. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, affixes the notarial seal, and issues the original and two certified copies to be presented to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Final notarized Acta Constitutiva and Reglamento
Founder's original passport or national ID
Registered agent's acceptance letter and registration undertaking
Signed initial endowment declaration with bank evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is refused due to incomplete identification, obtain a notarial act of non-appearance, cure the documentary defect, and re-appear before the same notary within 2 business days; the initial notarial fee is credited toward the final execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter, the two certified copies, the name-search certificate, and the official filing fee of approximately USD 250 at the Foundations Section. The registry examiner verifies compliance with Articles 5-9 of Law 25 of 1995. Upon approval the Foundation acquires legal personality; the registry issues a Copia Certificada de la Inscripción and a Certificate of Existence.
required_dossiers: Notarized Acta Constitutiva in original plus two certified copies
Name availability certificate
Official fee receipt issued by the Public Registry collection desk
Registered agent form and consent
Certified copy of the notarial power of attorney for the filing counsel, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files an observed defect or rejection, the filing attorney submits a written cure petition within 3 business days, accompanied by corrective pages and the corrected instrument. If the defect is not cured, the founding party may file a reconsideration request or a new expediente containing the corrected pages, preserving the priority of the submitted name and date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Installation of the Foundation Council and Adoption of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (Consejo de la Fundación) of the Private Interest Foundation, with the Registered Agent acting as keeper of the records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council in an organizational meeting or adopt a unanimous written consent to: confirm the subscription of the initial endowment and the issuance of participation certificates; approve the registered office at the agent's premises; elect the President, Secretary, and Treasurer; appoint the Protector, if designated; ratify the banking signatory authorities; approve the internal AML/KYC and record-keeping policy; and authorize the officers to file the maritime bunkering license applications described in the licensing module.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter and Certificate of Existence
First Board Resolution signed by all Foundation Councillors
Officer acceptance letters with specimen signatures
Participation certificate ledger
Protector acceptance letter, if applicable
AML/KYC and record-keeping policy approved by the Foundation Council
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a councillor cannot attend in person, the resolution is executed by unanimous written consent of all remaining councillors. If the Protector objects to any governance term, the President convenes an extraordinary Foundation Council meeting within 5 business days, with the Registered Agent present as witness; the meeting minutes cure the objection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (Panama Maritime Authority, AMP), whose Dirección Nacional de Empresas Navieras issues the bunkering operation authorization, coordinated with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for fuel commercialization registration and with the Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) for environmental licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Maritime Fuel Supply Operation License (Licencia de Operación para el Suministro de Combustible Marino a Buques – Bunkering), supplemented by an AMP vessel operation permit for bunkering lighters and a MICI fuel trader registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de la República de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, EsIA) is required when the operation includes shore-side fuel storage tanks, piers, or terminal infrastructure. Category I – Environmental Impact Form (Formulario de Impacto Ambiental) is available for ship-to-ship transfer-only bunkering using double-hull lighters without permanent shore-side installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Strict no-discharge rule for oil and oily mixtures in Panamanian territorial waters under MARPOL 73/78 Annex I and Law 41 of 1998 as implemented by MiAMBIENTE; treated bilge water may only be discharged through an oily-water separator with oil content not exceeding 15 ppm; marine fuel supplied must comply with the international sulphur cap of 0.50% m/m and NOx Tier II limits under MARPOL Annex VI Regulations 13-14; ballast water must be managed in accordance with the International Ballast Water Management Convention; all wastewater discharges to receptor bodies must meet the quality thresholds of Executive Decree No. 96 of 2014 and MiAMBIENTE receptor-water quality resolutions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for all fuel storage, transfer, and lightering points; structural load inspection and municipal occupancy certificate from the competent Municipality for any shore-side offices or tank farms; occupational health and safety clearance from MITRADEL under Executive Decree 168 of 1999; and AMP verification of marine safety management systems, crew certification, and third-party civil liability insurance for all bunkering craft and shore interfaces.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (TU@PA and Facturación Electrónica en Línea systems)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) by filing an online application through the DGI TU@PA portal or in person at DGI regional offices, accompanied by the registered foundation deed, the Public Registry incorporation certificate for the Private Interest Foundation, and a sworn statement designating a fiscal representative or resident agent for tax compliance. The DGI issues the RUC within 5 to 15 business days. For ITBMS purposes, the foundation must also activate its Taxpayer Registry status and obtain a digital certificate for electronic invoicing if it will conduct taxable activities in Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch elections. A Private Interest Foundation may elect to register as an ITBMS taxpayer and may further elect the Simplified Tax Regime (RTS) if annual gross income does not exceed B/.36,000. A foundation engaged in bunkering may elect to be treated as a regular juridical person under the Fiscal Code, thereby limiting tax exposure to Panama-source income and subjecting itself to standard ITBMS obligations. No irrevocable single-tier pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - known in Panama as ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 annual gross income threshold for the simplified small-taxpayer regime; otherwise all taxable persons performing taxable transfers or services in Panama are required to register with DGI regardless of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing under the Facturación Electrónica en Línea (FEL) system. Taxpayers must obtain DGI digital authorization before issuing invoices; each invoice must be transmitted to DGI in XML format through the authorized web service or commercial API, must contain a digital signature, and must display a DGI-generated QR code. Bunker fuel deliveries require the e-invoice to be transmitted within 24 hours of supply, with real-time fiscal clearance for each transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of marine fuel and lubricants to vessels engaged in international navigation, including deep-sea vessels on foreign routes and ships traversing the Panama Canal, qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate as export services when the bunker supplier is registered with DGI and the delivery is documented as an international supply. Services rendered to non-residents and consumed entirely outside Panama also qualify. The bunker supplier must obtain and retain evidence of the vessel's international voyage documentation and destination outside Panama.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Combustible) filed through Panama Customs SISPA
Bunkering Delivery Receipt (BDN) signed by the vessel master and bunker supplier
Bill of Lading or International Voyage Certificate evidencing the vessel's foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de remesa) or SWIFT confirmation evidencing foreign-currency payment from a non-Panamanian bank account
DGI-registered electronic invoice for the zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama's Fiscal Code and Tax Administrative Act impose a 50% surcharge on omitted ITBMS for unjustified zero-rating claims, together with graduated fines ranging from B/.500 to B/.10,000 and statutory interest. Repeated fraudulent zero-rating practices trigger criminal tax fraud liability under Article 29 of the Tax Criminal Code (Section 263-A), which carries imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and disqualification from holding tax registry authorizations. The DGI may retrospectively claw back VAT credits claimed on export supplies for up to six fiscal years and penalize the taxpayer for each false invoice issued.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama) is the principal banking, FX, and payment-system regulator for the Republic of Panama; Panama has no central bank and operates a fully dollarized monetary regime under Decree Law No. 16 of 1950 and Law No. 21 of 2017. The Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and clearing bank for the State but exercises no monetary policy or exchange-control powers. The Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Autoridad Marítima de Panamá apply ancillary controls over port-related commercial flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully convertible regime without capital-account or current-account controls. Panama has no exchange-control law, no convertibility permit system, and no restriction on profit remittance, dividend distribution, capital repatriation, or distribution of foundation benefits to non-residents. The US dollar is legal tender and the only settlement currency for balances; accounts may also be carried in major currencies, but the effective treasury is dollar-centered. Profit and benefit distributions are subject solely to AML/KYC verification and, where applicable, statutory tax formalities, not to any FX authorization. The legal risk profile for remittance of bunkering revenue is low from an FX-access standpoint and moderate from a compliance-verification standpoint.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panamanian law imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender window, no forced conversion ratio, and no requirement to deposit dollars with any state institution. Bunkering and refueling revenues may be retained in full in the operating treasury, credited to any bank in Panama, or reinvested abroad. The only obligations are statistical balance-of-payments reporting by licensed banks on an aggregate basis and the entity's AML obligations under Law 23 of 2015.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account (USD) with segregated Capital Funding Escrow sub-account for the PIF minimum endowment
Operational Treasury Account plus Standby LC and trade-finance account module
Operational Treasury Account with Commercial Letter of Credit facilitation for fuel imports
Operational account for port authority, Maritime Single Window, and licence fee disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore unlicensed e-money institutions have no legal passport into Panama; only Sociedades de Pago authorized by the Superintendency of Banks may lawfully provide payment services, and their scope is capped at payment initiation and e-money issuance without full treasury-grade account services. A marine bunkering treasury dependent on such providers would encounter correspondent-bank de-risking, OFAC screening fragility, and FATF-related reputational concern. All liquidity must reside in licensed banks, with foreign EMIs used only as a remittance front-end to a licensed Panamanian account where expressly permitted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or equivalent secure video-KYC identity verification is de facto mandatory for PIF signatories and ultimate beneficial owners classified as medium-risk enhanced. Panamanian banks in practice require a compliance interview with the founder, each council member, and the designated beneficiary; the interview may be virtual only where the bank maintains an international private-banking desk and apostilled/notarized identity documents are delivered by courier. A physical resident council member or local agent substantially accelerates onboarding and reduces the 'opening-committee' rejection rate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation opacity: the PIF legal form is perceived as an asset-hiding or shell vehicle without organic commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified and apostilled foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva) and regulations (Reglamento) as inscribed in the Public Registry, registry issuance certificate, duly sealed foundation-council appointment resolution, statutory beneficial-ownership declaration under Law 23 of 2015, sworn declaration of the council members waiving opacity, the RUC or specific tax-identification certificate of the foundation, local physical-office lease, local personnel contracts, and a written legal opinion confirming the PIF's capacity to contract, invoice, and hold the bunkering operating licence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bunkering and coastal marine-fuel sector historically exposed to vessel-to-vessel transfer opacity, sanctions evasion, product diversion, and smuggling
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid marine fueling operation licence from the Panama Maritime Authority, fuel-supplier registration or hydrocarbon permit from the National Energy Secretariat, commercial contracts with the terminal supplier, vessel purchase/order documents listing IMO numbers, port-call DVDs and AIS tracking records, signed delivery tickets with hydrostatic-tested quantity certification, export/import customs declarations, destination-port documentation, an entity-level AML/CTF policy incorporating the Panama Canal Area risk environment, and the statutory appointment of a compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency over the PIF capital endowment and pre-operating working capital received through cross-border wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign bank reference letters, three months of source-account statements for each funding wire, notarized deed of contribution identifying the transfer as endowment or working capital into PA_PIF, a declaration of source of wealth (sale of assets, inheritance, employment, or dividends) with supporting deeds or records, proof of the minimum US$10,000 subscribed capital with the instrument's paid-in tranche evidence, and a funding narrative pinpointing the commercial build-out of the bunkering operation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound contributions are routed exclusively by SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV wires to the PIF's USD account at a licensed Tier-1 Panamanian bank; the payment reference field must state 'Capital Contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF per Foundation Deed' and include the foundation RUC where assigned. For US-dollar legs landing through New York, the instructing bank must apply ABA routing, and the originator must be screened against OFAC/SDN, EU, UN, and Panamanian UAF lists before credit. The initial US$10,000 endowment is posted to a capital escrow sub-ledger; funds above this amount are allocated to the operational treasury only after the bank's enhanced due-diligence clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outflows for fuel purchases, tug services, port dues, and crew settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV in USD, settled principally through CHIPS or Fedwire correspondent networks. For high-value bunker supply commitments, the governing rail is an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued under ICC UCP 600 by the Panamanian bank as issuing bank, conveyed by SWIFT MT700, with MT707 for amendments and MT798 for related structured messages, supplemented by a Standby Letter of Credit to secure open-account replenishment agreements with terminals. All SWIFT references and UMR-related confirmation records are retained as the treasury audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC spot conversion contracts in freely convertible pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CHF/USD, JPY/USD) executed with licensed Panamanian banks or their offshore correspondent dealing desks without central authorization
Outright bilateral FX forwards of up to 12 months in non-USD pairs with a licensed bank or an OECD-resident counterparty bank under ISDA/SAC terms
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or emerging-market currencies (e.g., USD/CNY, USD/BRL, USD/COP) transacted through the bank's offshore treasury desk with full AML/EFT screening
Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR, USD/JPY) applied to match long-term bunker finance or equipment lease liabilities
Natural treasury hedging maintained by invoicing all bunker sales in USD while holding EUR and GBP concentration accounts that are actively sold into USD under standing spot orders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) for Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, filed through the Public Registry of Panama and the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 2 January through 15 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late surcharge with default interest; the foundation is recorded as 'en mora', loses access to good-standing certificates (Paz y Salvo), and continued default may lead to administrative penalties and eventual removal from the Public Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owners Registry Validation (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiarios Finales) and Special UBO Annual Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI, Registry of Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual validation aligned with franchise tax window (2 January - 15 March); supplementary UBO declaration required within 60 days after any transfer of foundation rights or change in beneficiary structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure to validate blocks issuance of good-standing status and subjects the PIF to fines plus the special UBO annual tax under Law 254 of 2021; willful misdeclaration can attract criminal sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta, Formulario 1322) - conditional on economic activity or Panama-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing surcharge, monthly default interest, and fines of up to USD 5,000 under the Panamanian Tax Code for non-filing or incorrect filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit applies to passive international PIFs; the DGI may require certified audited financial statements where Panama-source gross annual revenue exceeds USD 750,000, and a full audit is mandatory if the PIF operates a marine fuel concession in Panamanian waters, holds regulated banking or insurance licenses, or is ordered by the Public Registry or a court
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama; SMEs and qualifying PIFs may apply IFRS for SMEs; statutory records are kept in USD (currency of account) with Spanish-language statutory books

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual DGI validation of UBO records each January-March plus a mandatory declaration of any transfer of beneficiary rights, foundation assets, or protector and council changes within 60 days; the annual validation must identify natural persons who ultimately own or control 10% or more of foundation assets, otherwise a sworn statement of no identified UBO is filed
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes and Resolutions of the Foundation Council (Actas y Resoluciones)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,500 annual licensed registered agent; plus USD 150 - USD 500 for statutory office, bookkeeping and DGI compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 for a certified statutory audit, only where the audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: profits derived from foreign-source operations (including bunkering outside Panamanian waters) are exempt from Panama corporate tax. No statutory tax holiday for bunkering; the general corporate tax rate applies to Panamanian-source income. Available incentives include accelerated depreciation for fuel storage equipment and tax credits for investments in certain IT and logistics; the PIF is subject to an annual franchise tax of PAB 300 and can opt for a consolidated payment of PAB 2,000 under Law 25 for commercial operations, which acts as a minimum effective tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form DGI 110 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the Panama DGI ‘e-Tax 2.0’ system (www.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months after the fiscal-year close. For calendar-year filers the deadline is 31 March of the following year; any other fiscal year must file within the same three-month window. Requests for extension must be made on Form DGI 122, and approved extensions are granted only when the provisional tax is paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross receipts from the sale and delivery of marine fuel and lubricants to vessels in Panama’s ports, territorial waters, or the Canal watershed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income sourced within Panama. A PIF that operates as an offshore bunkering intermediary, with title to fuel passing outside Panamanian waters, is not subject to tax and should report nil in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1b — Foreign-source income and exempt income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report income from fuel supplied to vessels on the high seas, outside Panamanian jurisdiction, and any interest or royalties received from non-residents without a Panamanian nexus.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income is excluded from the taxable base. Non-resident managers must maintain a transfer pricing allocation memorandum demonstrating the siphon of revenue to foreign activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the excess of Panamanian-source gross income over the direct and apportioned costs, including the cost of aviation or marine fuel purchased, port fees, and logistics overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are permitted only if the underlying expenditures were subject to a 15% Panamanian tax deduction rule for services paid to local suppliers. The PIF must substantiate every deduction with invoices, contracts, and bank wires.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Multiply the resulting net taxable income by 25%, then apply any available tax credits, carryforwards, and the annual minimum corporate tax of PAB 1,000 for companies with gross income over PAB 100,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF has no Panamanian-source business and holds only foreign assets, this box must show zero. In all cases, the PIF must file the annual minimum tax return if it holds a Panama bank account or a registered office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed fine of PAB 500 to PAB 2,000 (greater for repeated breaches) plus 2% per month of the tax due, without exceeding 60% of the total tax. Late payment: a 10% surcharge, monthly 1% interest, and daily running penalty of PAB 20 per working day. Criminal evasion may lead to a fine equal to twice the tax evaded and imprisonment of 1–5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduced rate, the beneficial owner must be tax resident in the treaty country, obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its domestic tax authority, and deliver it to the Panamanian payor before the dividend payment. The payor must then complete Form DGI 150 and the DTA module in e-Tax 2.0, including a statement confirming the beneficial owner’s entitlement and absence of abusive holding structures. The TRC must cover the exact calendar year in which the income is paid and be apostilled when requested. Panama’s current DTAs (e.g., Spain, UK, Netherlands, Singapore, Mexico) require a minimum holding period (usually 12 months) for lower rates on dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest withholding is 10% for interest paid to a non-resident on a Panamanian-source debt (exempt if the lender is a foreign and/or Panamanian licensed bank and the loan is arm’s length; loans from the OECD Qualified Lending category are also exempt). Royalties for use of IP in Panama are subject to a 10% statutory withholding, with a 12.5% rate for technical assistance filings if the provider is a related party. Under DTAs, interest and royalties are generally reduced to 5% or 0% for interest and 5% or 10% for royalties; however, a defensive LOB clause may deny treaty benefits to a shell PIF.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 1,000,000 of aggregate related-party transactions in the fiscal year triggers the obligation to prepare and file the Local File; the Master File is mandatory when related-party transactions exceed PAB 5,000,000 or if the group’s consolidated gross revenue exceeds PAB 25,000,000. A separate informative return (Form DGI 243) is required for all related-party transactions exceeding PAB 250,000, in accordance with Resolution MT-148-2017.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (Law 35 of 2021) treat a bunkering operation as a 'logistics/distribution' relevant activity where the supply of fuel to vessels constitutes physical import, storage and distribution in Panama. The PIF must demonstrate economic substance by: (1) maintaining a physical office or using an approved agent with a fixed address; (2) employing local staff or outsourcing to a licensed service provider with at least two Panamanian activities; (3) generating income and expenses that are proportional to the bunkering volume; (4) holding board meetings in Panamanian territory at least annually; and (5) filing a substance declaration with the DGI. Foreign-owned PIFs cannot be passive holding companies with subcontracted operations that merely receive income; each contract must be signed in Panama and operational decisions must be made in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Panamanian-source bunkering receipts, issuing false invoices for fuel sold to vessels, or using the PIF as a conduit to move taxable revenues out of Panamanian ports without declaring them.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 2 to 5 times the evaded tax, surcharge of 20%, monthly interest at 1%, and criminal imprisonment for 1 to 5 years (Penal Code Articles 101–105, Fiscal Code Article 971).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, Foundation Council members, and any restructuring expert are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency and civil restitution; a court may impose travel bans, freezing orders on personal assets, and if the evasion exceeds PAB 1,000,000, a prison sentence up to 6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting bunkering activities from a mailbox/agent with no local office, employees, or management substance, despite the mandatory ESR applicable to logistics and distribution. This includes having a registered address only in a law firm’s building while revenues are booked in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty up to PAB 500,000; daily fine of PAB 10,000 for continued non-compliance; cancellation of the commercial license and registration; the PIF may be struck off after 30 days of non-compliance. Under Law 35 of 2021, false declarations attract a separate criminal fine of PAB 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The founder and council members are personally liable for the economic substance penalty; the Public Prosecutor may apply for a travel ban and attachment of the PIF’s bank accounts; if the empty shell is used to repatriate untaxed profits, a money-laundering conviction carries a 7 to 12-year sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local/Master File when the PAB 1,000,000 threshold is met, submitting documentation with incomplete banking evidence, or charging sub-optimal fuel margins to related shipping entities to erode Panamanian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may adjust the margin to the arm’s length benchmark and impose a penalty of 5% of the adjustment plus 10% annual interest; separate fine of PAB 25,000 for not filing Form DGI 243; serious violation is handled as a tax fraud offense with criminal fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who attest to false or non-existent transfer pricing documentation face civil liability for the full deficiency, professional disqualification for local service providers, and criminal imprisonment for 2 to 4 years for false corporate books. The court may also award restitution and prohibit departure from Panama until payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML (Money Laundering and Financing of Proliferation)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting third-party cash, bearer shares, or coded wire transfers for bunker fuel, failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with the Panamanian Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), or being involved in the supply of fuel to a flagged vessel subject to international sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 fines: PAB 100,000 up to PAB 1,000,000 per infringement; the Panama Maritime Authority may suspend or revoke the special bunkering license; the funds and assets involved are seized; if criminal laundering is established, sentence is 5 to 12 years in El Renacer Prison.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Foundation Council, beneficial owner, and any compliance officer designated by the PIF may be arrested, subject to pretrial detention, and have their assets seized. The law requires the PIF to appoint a local AML officer; if none is appointed, every council member is deemed to bear personal criminal responsibility. Travel bans and Interpol red notices are standard in these investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Treaty Relief / Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming a lower DTA dividend withholding rate using a TRC issued by a jurisdiction where the PIF’s ultimate owner is not resident, or channeling dividends through a PIF that lacks the economic substance to be a beneficial owner under the DTA Limitation on Benefits clause.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full statutory 10% withholding, secondary penalty of 50% of the under-withheld tax, and non-deductibility of the reproducing dividend; if the false TRC was intentional, the fiscal offence is a crime punishable by a fine equal to three times the detriment and imprisonment up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The council and any advisor who knowingly used a false TRC become jointly and severally liable for the tax, interest and penalties; they may face professional debarment, a travel ban during the administrative proceeding, and imprisonment for tax fraud. In the case of a non-resident beneficial owner using a Panama PIF purely to obtain treaty benefits, Panama treats the structure as an 'abusive conduit' and denies all treaty benefits under the BEPS minimum standard.
